item.title: Extract Text Between Two Delimiters Shell Commands
item.description:
“Extract Text Between Two Delimiters Shell Commands”

When processing text files or streams within a shell environment, a frequent requirement is to extract the segment that resides exclusively between a defined starting boundary (like “Here”) and an ending boundary (like “string”). Various utilities offer distinct approaches, each with trade-offs regarding regex flavor support, handling of multiple matches, and multi-line input.

Leveraging GNU grep with PCRE Lookarounds

GNU grep’s Perl Compatible Regular Expressions (-P flag) provide powerful zero-width assertions, specifically lookarounds, which allow matching based on context without including the context markers in the output.

item.title: Shell Command Techniques for Deleting Lines Matching Patterns in Files
item.description:
“Shell Command Techniques for Deleting Lines Matching Patterns in Files”

When manipulating configuration files, logs, or source code on a Unix-like system, the frequent requirement is to delete specific lines that match a given textual pattern. While the sed utility is often the first tool considered, several other utilities offer robust, sometimes faster, or more portable methods for achieving this line deletion. How can we select the best technique for script reliability and performance?

item.title: Shell Scripting: Efficiently Select Text Lines Between Two Delimiter Patterns
item.description:
“Shell Scripting: Efficiently Select Text Lines Between Two Delimiter Patterns”

How can one reliably extract only the lines situated strictly between two known textual markers, say, lines containing pattern1 and lines containing pattern2, while often excluding the markers themselves, using standard Unix tools like awk or sed?

This is a frequent requirement in log analysis, configuration file modification, and data extraction tasks. Various shell utilities offer compact solutions, each with subtle differences in how they handle the boundary markers.

item.title: Python: Effective Ways to Remove Text Accents & Diacritics
item.description:
“Python: Effective Ways to Remove Text Accents & Diacritics”

When working with text in Python, you’ll often encounter characters with diacritical marks (accents, umlauts, etc.) that need to be converted to their plain ASCII equivalents. This process, often called accent stripping or diacritic removal, is crucial for tasks like creating unique identifiers, performing case-insensitive searches, or ensuring compatibility across different systems.

Several methods exist in Python to achieve this, each with its own strengths and nuances. Let’s delve into these solutions with practical code examples.
